trials.claim: Each code limited to 5,000 monthly requests and 20 locations per account
trials.claimQuote: Each code comes with just 2 limitations: 5,000 monthly requests and 20 locations per account.
trials.reasoning: E1 only complains that a monthly review limit makes use infeasible; it does not confirm or deny the stated 5,000 requests and 20 locations per code.

exhibits.quote: Sure I can get a domain simply for this but for the limitation of reviews per month, this doesn't make it feasible.
exhibits.argument: Shows the monthly request limit makes agency use infeasible, undermining the claim it is just a minor limitation.

trials.claim: 5 codes gives 100 locations for 100 single-location clients to grow agency
trials.claimQuote: You get 100 locations (that's 100 single-location clients) to grow your agency.
trials.reasoning: E2 says a growing user may eventually offload clients or pay more, but it does not confirm or deny that 5 codes provide 100 locations for 100 single-location clients.

exhibits.quote: As eventually you'll either have to offload clients or pay them more to keep them all there.
exhibits.argument: Shows the location allowance cannot sustain growing client numbers without offloading or paying more, undermining the 100-client growth claim.

trials.claim: New resource-intensive features may require adding own API key or third-party service
trials.claimQuote: Yes. If a new feature is resource-intensive, we'll give you the option to add your own API key or connect a third-party service under your own account.
trials.reasoning: E3 describes built-in SMTP via Mailgun for email sending, which does not address whether future resource-intensive features may require your own API key or third-party service.

exhibits.quote: I ran into a small snag trying to connect Amazon SES for SMTP, but then I found out it includes built-in SMTP via Mailgun, which made things a lot easier.
exhibits.argument: Shows resource-intensive sending is expected to be included built-in, undermining the claim buyers should supply their own key or service.

trials.claim: Needing more requests or locations requires subscription upgrade while keeping paid usage
trials.claimQuote: You will need to upgrade your subscription, but keep the existing usage you paid for.
trials.reasoning: E4 says users may offload clients or pay more to keep them, but it does not show whether an upgrade preserves the usage already paid for.

exhibits.quote: As eventually you'll either have to offload clients or pay them more to keep them all there.
exhibits.argument: Shows exceeding limits forces offloading clients, contradicting the promise that paid usage is kept when upgrading.

trials.claim: AI reputation management gets you more five star reviews automatically
trials.claimQuote: AI reputation management that gets you more five star reviews, automatically.
trials.reasoning: The vendor homepage promises autopilot review requests and more 5-star ratings, and a buyer reports Google reviews skyrocketing in real use. The prosecution exhibits show some people do not complete reviews, but do not materially contradict that result.

exhibits.quote: I have it directed to my google review site but I find many people only click the face and dont fill out the google review.
exhibits.argument: Shows the tool does not automatically convert interactions into five-star reviews.

exhibits.quote: More Good Reviews is superior and more polished than these competitors, but lacks this feature.
exhibits.argument: Shows the product lacks the requested AI-generated review process, undermining the automatic AI reputation claim.

exhibits.quote: Request reviews on autopilot. Get more 5-star ratings. Rank higher than your competition.
exhibits.argument: The vendor's own homepage promises autopilot review requests that get more 5-star ratings.

exhibits.quote: I'm using it at the hair salon, and google reviews are skyrockeitng!
exhibits.argument: The buyer confirms the product actually increased their Google reviews in real use.

trials.claim: 5 codes required to unlock agency white label plan
trials.claimQuote: You need 5 codes to unlock the agency white label plan.
trials.reasoning: E7 and E8 complain about CNAME and custom-domain setup problems, but neither confirms nor denies that 5 codes are required to unlock the agency white label plan.

exhibits.quote: I wanted to like this for its simplicity until I got to the agency setup. You'll be forced to use cnames that they want.
exhibits.argument: Shows the agency white-label setup is restrictive and problematic, undermining the unlock value claim.

exhibits.quote: The Proxy is already turned off in cloudflare, and the error is still happening.
exhibits.argument: Shows the white-label custom domain CNAME integration fails, undermining the agency white-label promise.

themes.summary: Several buyers say the founder and team reply fast, fix issues within hours, and guide onboarding.

hits.quote: thanks to the founder Scott Vayner for taking the time to answer my questions before I bought the software
Amazing guidance on the onboarding when it comes to the set up.
In addition, the customer is very responsive and does an excellent job.
Scott (the owner) had it done within hours!
four hours later, they had applied a fix and responded to my email.

themes.summary: Many users say the tool collects reviews, displays widgets, and automates requests reliably and easily.

hits.quote: It does that job really well and was easy to set up.
Does everything I need it to do.
The product is very useful for getting additional reviews
It supports several strategies to coax responses from customers without irritating them.
Set up was a breeze, took me a bit to figure out how to setup the CNAM on Cloudflare

themes.summary: Several buyers call it a deep-value, no-brainer deal worth more than charged.

hits.quote: they should consider charging WAY MORE for what they are giving.
If it ever comes back do not hesitate to buy it.

themes.summary: Several users complain about forced CNAMEs and limited control over review display.

hits.quote: I would like to see a little more display control on the review landing page.
My only real gripes at the moment would be the lack of ability to properly display reviews effectively in my website
You'll be forced to use cnames that they want.

themes.summary: A few users report CNAME setup failures and reviews being recorded before Google submission.

hits.quote: The CNAME integration is still pending.
I wish it didnt record the review until that was entered.

hits.quote: for the limitation of reviews per month, this doesn't make it feasible.
